content:
According to reports, Apple will unveil its first foldable iPhone in just over two weeks. Despite potentially being branded as the "iPhone Ultra" with a price tag exceeding US$2,000, the device will come with several major limitations.

1. Telephoto Lens

Reportedly, the iPhone Ultra will feature two cameras, including a main lens and an ultra-wide lens, and is not expected to include a telephoto lens. For many, this may be the biggest design limitation of the device.

The main lens and ultra-wide lens of the iPhone Ultra are both expected to be 48-megapixel, similar to the existing iPhone 17 base model.

2. Action Button

According to multiple leaked iPhone Ultra dummy units, the device will not feature an Action Button. It appears this will be the first iPhone in Apple's history to come with absolutely no mute switch.

The dummy units show that the left side of the device's frame is completely blank. Reportedly, the side button and camera control button will be located on the right side of the iPhone Ultra's frame, while the volume buttons will be positioned on the top edge of the device, similar to the iPad mini.

3. Face ID

The iPhone Ultra is not expected to feature Face ID, and will instead adopt Touch ID built into the side button. This will be the first iPhone without Face ID since Apple first introduced Face ID on the iPhone X in 2017.

The likely reason the iPhone Ultra may adopt Touch ID instead of Face ID is the device's extremely slim design. Additionally, using Face ID would require Apple to include two sets of Face ID components, one for the outer display and one for the inner display.

Apple currently still uses Touch ID built into the power button on most iPads, including the basic iPad, iPad mini, and iPad Air.

4. MagSafe

Unless Apple surprises us, the iPhone Ultra looks set to forgo support for MagSafe wireless charging. Leaked iPhone Ultra dummy units do not display a MagSafe magnetic ring on the back.

The iPhone Ultra may support standard wireless charging similar to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8. However, based on current rumours, the chances of supporting MagSafe seem slim.

5. Physical SIM Card

Sources including Ming-Chi Kuo and Bloomberg have indicated that the iPhone Ultra will adopt an eSIM-only design globally.

This is likely also due to the foldable iPhone's extremely slim design. The iPhone Air is similarly extremely slim and has already adopted an eSIM-only design globally. As for the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro, they have adopted an eSIM-only design in the US and some other countries, but still retain a physical SIM card slot in markets such as China.

Summary

Without a doubt, Apple's foldable iPhone Ultra will come with several major trade-offs. The question is whether the practicality of this innovative foldable design will be enough to compensate for the aforementioned limitations.

Personally, I'm very much looking forward to trying out the iPhone Ultra for myself. The trade-off I'm most concerned about is the lack of MagSafe. I'm currently using an iPhone Air, so I'm already used to life without a telephoto lens, and I'm confident I could adapt to Touch ID fairly quickly. However, my home is filled with MagSafe chargers everywhere, so switching to regular wireless charging or all-day wired charging would be a major adjustment.

What are your thoughts? Feel free to head over to the comments section to let us know.
